TR89.title: Nissan Technical Review No.89 (2023), New X-TRAIL feature

TR90.title: Nissan Technical Review No.90 (2024), Special Feature 1: Electrification

statements.quantity: steady-state operation point at the best thermal efficiency
statements.value: 2000 rpm; minimum brake specific fuel consumption 217 g/kWh
about 2350 rpm before; changed to 2000 rpm

statements.quantity: share of operating time at the best fuel-efficiency point
statements.value: more than 80 % of the operating time in the WLTC plus Extra High mode (Fig. 7)
statements.procedure: WLTC plus Extra High test mode, not in-use driving
statements.comparability: procedure-bound: not comparable to all-driving share; C1 pre-labelled not comparable (M703 Rev 1 item 4)

statements.quantity: lowest engine speed used in the e-POWER operating points
statements.value: engine speeds below 1500 rpm are not utilised (exhaust system designed for this)
106 kW at 4400 rpm (domestic market), compression ratio 8.0

statements.quantity: engine start frequency against vehicle speed (Fig. 6, practical driving pattern)
statements.value: starts are made less frequent at low speed where engine noise exceeds road noise and more frequent at high speed; compared with a second-generation compact car, starts are reduced in the 20 to 40 km/h range and increased in the 40 to 60 km/h range
statements.comparability: qualitative direction by speed range; comparison vehicle is a different car

statements.quantity: engine start trigger at low load and low speed
statements.value: the engine starts because of a decrease in SOC in a low-load, low-speed scenario (engine speed then lowered for quietness)

statements.quantity: acceleration that avoids engine starts in the EV mode
statements.value: about 0.15 G, below about 30 km/h (figure read in the text)

statements.quantity: battery assist with the turbocharged engine
statements.value: in the new X-TRAIL system e-POWER is combined with a turbocharged engine for the first time; the battery-assist function is used actively and coordinated with the rise in boost pressure to avoid stagnant acceleration (Fig. 19)
statements.comparability: the document's assist is an acceleration-response (turbo-lag) function, not the engine-start trigger

statements.quantity: engine dedicated to e-POWER, best BSFC and maximum-power speeds
statements.value: optimum BSFC operating point at 2000 to 2400 rpm; maximum output at 4800 rpm
statements.applies: a different, dedicated engine concept for a 50 % thermal-efficiency target, NOT the X-TRAIL VC-TURBO engine
statements.comparability: must not be mixed with S1 to S5 (4400 rpm and 2000 rpm are the X-TRAIL values)
